data.gender_notes: Girishwar is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Giri means mountain and Ishwar means Lord. This name is derived from Hindu mythology and refers to Lord Shiva, who is often depicted as living in the mountains. It is a name of great power and reverence. The name Girishwar carries the meaning “Lord of the Mountain” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Girishwar usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of the mountain and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes strength, resilience, and connection to nature.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Girishwar" holds deep cultural significance in Hinduism as it is associated with Lord Shiva, the destroyer and the transcender, who is worshiped as the supreme god in charge of the cyclic course of destruction in the universe. He is the god of fertility, regeneration, and purification. The mountain symbolizes the masculine divine principle and the abode of the gods.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hinduism, Lord Shiva, represented by the name "Girishwar," is known for his three essential aspects: the creator (as Brahma), the preserver (as Vishnu), and the destroyer (as Shiva). He is the one who inherently embodies the three aspects of creation, preservation, and transformation in the universe. His presence in the mountains signifies detachment, purity, and the ultimate connection with the divine. People who bear this name are believed to possess the unwavering strength of Lord Shiva, and his spirit of creation, preservation, and transformation.
